To identify a speaker’s mood (emotion) from conversation, the supplied results indicate that using only a limited window of recent turns can capture most of the performance gain. In causal emotion recognition in conversation, performance is dominated by conversational context and “saturates quickly,” with roughly 90% of the gain captured within the most recent 10–30 preceding turns (depending on the label set) [1].

Regarding sentence starters, the supplied work does not directly study sentence starters as a factor for identifying mood. However, it does analyze discourse-level patterns and marker position: it finds a reliable association between emotion and discourse-marker position, with sadness showing reduced left-periphery marker usage compared to other emotions [1]. It also reports that hierarchical sentence representations help most in utterance-only settings but lose advantage once turn-level context is available, suggesting later conversational history can subsume effects that might otherwise come from sentence-level structure [1].
